_note: Original setting-specific backgrounds for Open Dungeon Master. Not SRD-derived content. Skills are ids from src/lib/srd/skills.json.

backgrounds.name: Corpo Dropout
backgrounds.featureDesc: You still hold a valid corporate ID from your old employer. It gets you past lobby security and into the lower floors of any megacorp tower, and a former colleague will still take your call, though not risk their job for you.
backgrounds.blurb: You walked out of a megacorp tower with insider skills, a few secrets, and a target on your back.

backgrounds.name: Street Doc
backgrounds.featureDesc: You know where to find unlicensed care in any district, and its staff will treat you and your crew first, discreetly, and on credit. In return you are expected to bring business and keep quiet about what you see.
backgrounds.blurb: You patch up runners in an unlicensed clinic. No questions, credits up front, favors remembered.

backgrounds.name: Fixer's Runner
backgrounds.featureDesc: Half the undercity owes you a small favor or is owed one. Once per session you can call one in: a safe room for the night, a name, a ride, or a package moved without questions.
backgrounds.blurb: You moved packages and secrets for a fixer; half the undercity owes you or is owed by you.

backgrounds.name: Arcology Rat
backgrounds.featureDesc: You can find a maintenance route into or through any arcology or corporate block that others would miss. When you lead the party through the ducts, you travel between two points in the structure twice as fast.
backgrounds.blurb: You grew up in the maintenance ducts of an arcology and know every vent, camera blind spot, and cargo lift.

backgrounds.name: Chrome Pit Fighter
backgrounds.featureDesc: Fight crowds remember your handle. In any gym, cage or betting den you can find a place to sleep, a meal and a sparring partner, and a promoter will always have work for a fighter with a name.
backgrounds.blurb: You fought augmented brawlers in the cage circuit, and the crowds still chant your handle.

backgrounds.name: Data Courier
backgrounds.featureDesc: You know the couriers' dead drops and handshakes. You can leave or collect a message or a small package in any city without meeting the other party, and no one can trace it to you.
backgrounds.blurb: You carried encrypted payloads through hostile grid sectors, sometimes in your own headware.

backgrounds.name: Guild Engineer
backgrounds.featureDesc: Your guild card is honored in any workshop, foundry or engineering hall. You can borrow tools and a bench, read the guild's blueprints, and expect lodging from a fellow member, provided your dues are paid.
backgrounds.blurb: A certified member of the engineers' guild, welcome in any workshop and fluent in blueprints.

backgrounds.name: Airship Deckhand
backgrounds.featureDesc: Every port tower has someone who crewed with you. You can secure passage on an airship for yourself and your companions in exchange for working the rigging, and you hear the gossip of the docks before it reaches the ground.
backgrounds.blurb: You crewed a trade airship, splicing rigging in gales and trading gossip in every port tower.

backgrounds.name: Clockwork Apprentice
backgrounds.featureDesc: Having wound and repaired a master's automata, you can tell at a glance how a clockwork device is meant to work, where its maker hid the override, and whether it has been tampered with.
backgrounds.blurb: You served a master artificer, winding automata and learning which gears hide the maker's tricks.

backgrounds.name: Union Stoker
backgrounds.featureDesc: The laborers' union counts you as family. Its halls will feed and hide you, its stokers pass you word of what moves through the engine rooms, and a picket line will open for you.
backgrounds.blurb: You shoveled coal in the great engine halls, and the laborers' union still counts you as family.

backgrounds.name: Aether Scholar
backgrounds.featureDesc: Your academy name gets you into any symposium, salon or laboratory. Scholars will hear you out, share their notes, and put you up for a night, expecting a lecture in return.
backgrounds.blurb: You studied the aether sciences at a famous academy and can talk your way into any symposium.

backgrounds.name: Constabulary Inspector
backgrounds.featureDesc: Your retired warrant card still turns heads. Constables will speak to you as a colleague, show you a case file if asked quietly, and overlook a minor infraction, unless their captain is watching.
backgrounds.blurb: You walked a beat and closed cases for the city constabulary before turning in your badge.

backgrounds.name: Vault Born
backgrounds.featureDesc: You were taught from the old world's books. You can read pre-war signage, manuals and maps, and you know what a ruin was for and where its stores, generators and exits should be.
backgrounds.blurb: Raised in a sealed shelter on old-world books and drills, you stepped outside knowing everything but the wasteland.

backgrounds.name: Wasteland Scavenger
backgrounds.featureDesc: You can tell worthwhile salvage from scrap at a glance. When you search a ruin, you find the parts, fuel and provisions others overlook, and you know which merchant will pay for them.
backgrounds.blurb: You strip ruins for parts and provisions, and you can tell worthwhile salvage from scrap at a glance.

backgrounds.name: Caravan Guard
backgrounds.featureDesc: Every waystation and caravanserai on the routes you guarded knows your face. You and your companions can expect a meal, a bunk and the latest news of the road wherever a caravan stops.
backgrounds.blurb: You escorted traders between settlements, and every waystation on the route knows your face.

backgrounds.name: Cult Escapee
backgrounds.featureDesc: You can recite the congregation's liturgy and signs well enough to pass as one of the faithful. Cultists take you for a believer until you give them reason not to.
backgrounds.blurb: You fled a doomsday congregation and can still recite its liturgy well enough to pass as faithful.

backgrounds.name: Rad-Zone Guide
backgrounds.featureDesc: You read the wasteland the way sailors read weather. When you lead the party, you sense storms, radiation and hostile ground before they reach you, and you can always find a route around them.
backgrounds.blurb: You lead travelers through glowing craters and storm fronts, reading hazards the way sailors read weather.

backgrounds.name: Settlement Medic
backgrounds.featureDesc: You can tell at a glance who is dying, who is faking and what killed the ones who did not make it. Settlements will shelter a medic, and their people will bring you what supplies they have.
backgrounds.blurb: You kept a settlement alive with scavenged medicine and steady hands when the raiders came.

backgrounds.name: Grave Digger
backgrounds.featureDesc: You know every graveyard's layout and which graves are best left alone. The dead do not rise on ground you have tended, and church wardens will shelter you among the tombs.
backgrounds.blurb: You tend the churchyard and its dead, and you know which graves are best left undisturbed.

backgrounds.name: Asylum Survivor
backgrounds.featureDesc: Having been locked away for telling the truth, you can tell when someone is lying about what they have seen, and other survivors of the veil will speak with you when they will speak with no one else.
backgrounds.blurb: They locked you away for what you claimed to see. You were right, and you learned to read people to get out.

backgrounds.name: Occult Librarian
backgrounds.featureDesc: You remember where the worst books are shelved. In any library or archive you can find the restricted collection, and you know which volume holds the answer, though not always the cost of reading it.
backgrounds.blurb: You catalogued books that should not exist and remember exactly where the worst ones are shelved.

backgrounds.name: Seance Medium
backgrounds.featureDesc: You can hold a sitting for the grieving. Usually it is theater, and it pays. Sometimes something answers, and when it does, you are the one it speaks through.
backgrounds.blurb: You hold sittings for the grieving. Most nights it is theater; some nights something answers.

backgrounds.name: Cursed Bloodline
backgrounds.featureDesc: Your family name is known. It opens doors among those who fear it and closes them among those who know what it means, and once per session it turns aside a threat that would rather not cross your kin.
backgrounds.blurb: Your family name opens doors and ends conversations; everyone has heard what happens to your kin.

backgrounds.name: Night Watchman
backgrounds.featureDesc: You still carry a ring of keys and know which doors they open. After dark you can move through the town unchallenged, and you notice what has changed since your last round.
backgrounds.blurb: You walked the town's streets after dark with a lantern and a ring of keys, and you noticed things.

backgrounds.name: Private Inquiry Agent
backgrounds.featureDesc: Your ledger holds half the town's secrets. Once per session you can consult it for a fact about a local person of standing: a debt, an affair, a grudge, or who they were seen with.
backgrounds.blurb: You take discreet cases for paying clients, and your ledger holds half the town's secrets.

backgrounds.name: Beat Reporter
backgrounds.featureDesc: A press card opens doors that stay shut to strangers. Officials, witnesses and the wealthy will grant you an interview, and printers will run what you bring them.
backgrounds.blurb: You chase stories for the local paper, and a press card opens doors that stay shut to strangers.

backgrounds.name: Reformed Burglar
backgrounds.featureDesc: You see every building as a puzzle of latches and sight lines. Given a minute to look, you can say how a place is secured, where its blind spots are, and how you would have gotten in.
backgrounds.blurb: You went straight years ago, but you still see every house as a puzzle of latches and sight lines.

backgrounds.name: Courtroom Clerk
backgrounds.featureDesc: You know where every record is buried. In any courthouse, registry or archive you can find the deed, the will or the filing that matters, and the clerks let you look.
backgrounds.blurb: You filed the town's suits and wills for years, and you know where every record is buried.

backgrounds.name: Disgraced Socialite
backgrounds.featureDesc: Scandal cost you your standing, not your memory. You know the guest lists, the grudges and the back stairs of every great house, and a servant or a faded friend will still let you in.
backgrounds.blurb: Scandal cost you your standing, but you still know the guest lists, the grudges, and the back stairs.

backgrounds.name: Police Informant
backgrounds.featureDesc: The precinct and the street both think you are theirs. You can get a message to either side, and each will tell you what the other is planning, as long as neither learns you asked.
backgrounds.blurb: You traded whispers to the law to stay free, and both the precinct and the street think you are theirs.

backgrounds.name: Plague Doctor
backgrounds.featureDesc: Guards still let your mask through the barricades. You can enter and leave sealed districts, and the sick and their families will tell a plague doctor what they tell no one else.
backgrounds.blurb: You walked sealed districts in beak and wax, and guards still let your mask through the barricades.

backgrounds.name: Witch Hunter's Ward
backgrounds.featureDesc: You can read the order's trail signs and warrants. You know where the hunters have been, whom they are after, and how to pass yourself off as one of their wards when it counts.
backgrounds.blurb: Raised by an order that burns the unclean, you can read their trail signs and their warrants.

backgrounds.name: Penitent Pilgrim
backgrounds.featureDesc: Keepers of wayside shrines shelter penitents. On any pilgrim road you can find a shrine that offers you and your companions food, a roof, and word of who passed before you.
backgrounds.blurb: You walk the old pilgrim roads atoning for something, and keepers of wayside shrines shelter you.

backgrounds.name: Sellsword Deserter
backgrounds.featureDesc: You know your old company's signs, camps and habits. You can spot its members, predict how it fights, and find its quartermasters, but they know your name and want the desertion settled.
backgrounds.blurb: You abandoned a mercenary company that does not forgive. You know their ways, and they know your name.

backgrounds.name: Crypt Scribe
backgrounds.featureDesc: The wardens of the great necropolis still admit you. You can enter the tombs, read the funerary rites carved there, and learn what the dead were buried with and why.
backgrounds.blurb: You copied epitaphs and funerary rites in the great necropolis, and its wardens still admit you.

backgrounds.name: Beggar Prophet
backgrounds.featureDesc: The desperate who hear you preach bring you rumors and bread. In any city you can gather a small congregation within a day, and they will pass you what the streets are saying.
backgrounds.blurb: You preach doom on street corners, and the desperate who listen bring you rumors and bread.
